questions.q: Give an account of the major international conventions dealing with the environment.
answer: Several international conventions have been signed to protect different aspects of the environment.

answer.text: The Convention on Biological Diversity, adopted at the Rio Earth Summit of 1992, aims to conserve biodiversity, use it sustainably and share its benefits fairly, through the Cartagena and Nagoya protocols. CITES of 1973 regulates international trade in endangered species, while the Ramsar Convention of 1971 protects wetlands.

The Basel Convention controls the movement of hazardous wastes across borders, the Rotterdam Convention governs trade in hazardous chemicals, and the Stockholm Convention of 2001 targets persistent organic pollutants.
The Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol protect the ozone layer, while the UNFCCC, the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement address climate change.

answer: Together these treaties form a global framework for protecting the environment.

questions.q: What were the aims and outcomes of the Earth Summit and later climate conferences?

answer.text: have tried to build agreement on protecting the global environment.

list: The 1992 Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro brought nations together and produced agreements on climate change and biodiversity, and Agenda 21 for sustainable development
It established the principle that all nations share responsibility but developed nations, having polluted more, must do more
The Kyoto Protocol set binding targets for developed countries to cut greenhouse gases
The Paris Agreement got nearly all nations to pledge action to keep global warming well below dangerous levels

questions.q: What is the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities' in environmental agreements?

answer.text: is a cornerstone of international environmental agreements, recognising that not all countries are equally to blame for environmental damage.

list: All nations share a common responsibility to protect the global environment
But their responsibilities differ according to their contribution to the problem and their ability to act

answer.lead: It is a matter of fairness.

list: Developed countries, having caused most historical pollution and being richer, must take the lead in cutting emissions and provide funds and technology
Developing countries, still fighting poverty, are given more time and support to act
